title.narrative: Preparing for Data driven healthcare in Sub-Saharan Africa

description.narrative: Fragmented care delivery, increase of chronic illnesses, lack of ICT based information systems and inefficiencies in existing referral systems puts exponential pressure on resources of hospitals in African countries and leads to unequal distribution of access to healthcare as well as unnecessary revenue losses. Implementing Health Information Systems (eHIS) has the potential to strongly improve access to healthcare and improve (cash) management of health facilities. Africa eHealth Solutions International is an impact driven Dutch company that searches to contribute to the development of the African health sector and its mission is to create affordable quality care for all. To introduce and scale-up data driven e-health services in African countries, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to Pilot a e-hospital system through a comprehensive hospital system that includes Mobile App health services. Patients have a personal App and can communicate with the hospital, track their own health, upload vitals, lab values like blood sugar and receive educational material. The hospital can monitor the patients, including follow up on the tasks to be done. This encourages proper health seeking behaviour, awareness on preventive health and makes health services more economic. This project is highly relevant in view of the tremendous negative impact of non-communicable diseases in Africa ( 40% of mortality and 50% of co-morbidity in Kenya).The main purpose of the project was to obtain more experience on both the comprehensive hospital and mobile Application in order to develop a bankable business plan and prepare for further investments in selected countries. The project included market scans, partner search, training of staff, purchase of equipment and market testing through 5 test sites with existing hospitals. The project supported 16 direct jobs, 36 indirect jobs and provided knowledge transfer to 16 people regarding the development and implementation of e-health services and software. Furthermore, the test sites provided improved access to healthcare for 900 people. The pilot was successful and further investments in Kenya, Ghana, Zambia, Malawi and South Africa are currently being prepared. The ambition is to open 300-400 sites in the next 5 years, which will provide improved access to healthcare to over 10 million people.
